problem: Determine the largest union of intervals on which the function $f(x)=\frac{x-{x}^{2}}{7x}$ is continuous.
worked_solution:
This is a rational function, so it is continuous at all points in its domain. To find its domain, we start by factoring the numerator:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{x-{x}^{2}}{7x} \\  & =\frac{x(1-x)}{7x} \\  & =\frac{1-x}{7},\end{aligned}
$$

 

where $x\ne 0.$

This function is continuous everywhere except at the excluded point $x=0.$

Therefore, the domain consists of the union of the intervals $(-\infty ,0),$ and $(0,\infty ),$ namely

$$
(-\infty ,0)\cup (0,\infty )
$$

and the function is also continuous on this union of intervals.
